nodes.description: Contract owner address state variable, set to msg.sender in constructor and used as beneficiary of the 5 finney registration fee.
Mapping of address to uint pending withdrawal balances; accumulates rewards and registration fees.
Signed integer tracking the current tournament round, incremented in userRegister.
Counter of players registered in the current round, capped at 4.
mapping(int => address[7]) holding the seven participants of each round.
Constructor initializing owner to msg.sender, round to 1 and registered to 0.
View function returning the pending withdrawal balance of a given player.
View function returning the participant arrays of the previous and current round.
Withdraw function that zeroes the caller balance then transfers it, using a low-level address transfer.
Payable registration function charging 105 finney, updating participants and round state and triggering calcWinner.
Private function selecting a pseudo-random winner between two participants using blockhash and awarding a reward.
External caller identity, attacker-controlled, used for ownership, registration and withdrawal.
msg.sender.transfer(amount) external value call performed in userWithdraw, an unchecked low-level send to an untrusted address.
Address parameter of publicGetBalance used to index the withdrawals mapping.
Index of the first participant passed to calcWinner.
Index of the second participant passed to calcWinner.
Index of the participant slot where the winner is stored in calcWinner.
Reward amount in wei credited to the winning participant's withdrawal balance.
Local variable in userWithdraw caching withdrawals[msg.sender] before the transfer.
Local pseudo-random value derived from blockhash and participant addresses in calcWinner.

edges.reason: owner state variable is assigned from the untrusted msg.sender during construction.
msg.sender indexes the withdrawals mapping in userWithdraw and userRegister credit logic.
userWithdraw reaches the external transfer sink, allowing control flow to an untrusted address.
The transferred amount is derived from the withdrawals balance, making state and value flow converge at the external call.
Local amount variable, read from withdrawals[msg.sender], flows directly into the transfer.
The recipient of the transfer is the untrusted msg.sender.
userRegister conditionally invokes calcWinner when registered equals 1 or 3.
userRegister credits 5 finney to withdrawals[owner] on each registration.
userRegister writes the caller address into participants[round][registered].
userRegister increments or resets the registered counter.
userRegister increments the round variable when registered reaches 4.
calcWinner reads and writes participants[round][first/second/winner].
calcWinner adds the reward to withdrawals[participants[round][winner]].
calcWinner indexes participants using the current round variable.
publicGetBalance reads withdrawals[player].
publicGetState reads participants for the previous and current round.
publicGetState uses round and round-1 as mapping keys.
player parameter is used as the lookup key in publicGetBalance.
first parameter indexes participants inside calcWinner.
second parameter indexes participants inside calcWinner.
winner parameter indexes the participants slot written by calcWinner.
reward parameter is added to the winner's withdrawals balance.
participant addresses are cast to uint and combined into the local random value.
msg.sender is stored as a participant during userRegister.
calcWinner reads the round state variable to index participants.

normalization_plan.reason: The player parameter is only a lookup key for the withdrawals/session query and carries no independent security semantics.
The first index parameter is purely an argument of calcWinner and should be folded into that function node.
The second index parameter is purely an argument of calcWinner and should be folded into that function node.
The winner index parameter only selects a storage slot written by calcWinner and is a local detail of that function.
The reward parameter only determines the amount added to withdrawals inside calcWinner.
The local amount variable is the direct value argument of msg.sender.transfer and should be merged into the unsafe operation node.
The random local is computed and consumed entirely inside calcWinner to decide the payout branch.
